mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses equity discount rates and increases liquidity, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and economic support.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 2 months), or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand and housing market distress, which reduces household wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a coefficient not statistically significant (p>0.05) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a high labor market tightness regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals an impending labor market slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC for the PAYEMS decline signal in the high labor market tightness regime is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 3 months indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO increased over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC for INDPRO over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1350.0 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in the housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods (HOUST < 1350.0 for 2 months), or the Rank IC for the HOUST threshold condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% year-over-year and an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals persistent inflation and aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) does not produce negative 60-day returns in at least 60% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a coefficient not statistically significant (p>0.05) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 100.0), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening economy that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO declines and INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO decline signal in the industrial contraction regime is below 0.02.
